records.text: For the end, among psalms. A song of David.
records.prior_reason: The general for-the-end and Davidic song heading has no distinctive named occasion or other sufficiently specific correspondence established here; shared authorship alone is not credited.

records.text: Know that the Lord has made His holy one wondrous; the Lord will hear me when I cry to Him.
records.prior_reason: The Lord making His holy one wondrous and hearing the speaker's cry is read in context, but the holy one's identity is not supplied beyond this wording and no distinct target identification is established.

records.text: For the end, concerning her who inherits. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The heading concerning her who inherits leaves its feminine referent unnamed. An identification with a particular woman, congregation or later community would exceed the supplied title.

records.text: Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry.
records.prior_reason: The request to hear words and understand the cry is part of the opening petition, but a further link based only on a general request to hear prayer would add no sufficiently particular comparison.

records.text: Attend to the voice of my petition, my King and my God, for unto Thee I will pray, Lord.
records.prior_reason: The address my King and my God and attention to petition is read, but a shared divine title and generic prayer address alone do not establish an additional retained relationship.

records.text: For Thou wilt bless the righteous one; Lord, Thou didst crown us as with a weapon of favor.
records.prior_reason: The line crowns the worshippers as with a weapon of favor. A familiar rendering about surrounding someone with a shield is not substituted, and no adequately specific comparison for the actual crowning-and-weapon formulation is established.

records.text: Return, Lord; rescue my soul. Save me for the sake of Thy mercy.
records.prior_reason: The request for return, rescue and salvation for mercy's sake is read with the bodily lament, but no additional sufficiently particular target beyond a general rescue petition is established for this unit.

records.text: The Lord heard my petition; the Lord accepted my prayer.
records.prior_reason: The declaration that God heard and accepted the petition completes the lament's turn toward confidence. Generic answered-prayer counterparts are not added merely to credit the repeated assurance.

records.text: May all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; may they turn back and be greatly put to shame quickly.
records.prior_reason: The wish for enemies' shame, disturbance and quick retreat is read as the lament's conclusion; no particular enemy event or sufficiently distinct additional counterpart is established.

records.text: A psalm of David, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Chousi son of Iemeni.
records.prior_reason: The title names Chousi son of Iemeni. The separately read Hushai the Archite account does not establish this person's identity; the different supplied names and identifying descriptions remain unresolved.

records.text: Lord my God, in Thee I hoped. Save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,
records.prior_reason: The proposed Saul narrative shares a general plea for rescue from pursuit, but this unit does not identify Saul or supply an additional sufficiently distinctive correspondence. The comparison was removed after the complete-triple reread; the source remains pending.

records.text: then may the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, trample my life into the earth, and make my glory dwell in dust. Diapsalma.
records.prior_reason: The pursuit, trampling and dust form the consequence of the preceding conditional innocence oath. This full consequence was read as necessary context, but no separate particular counterpart is established merely from its grammatical continuation of that oath.

records.text: and an assembly of peoples will surround Thee; and for its sake return on high.
records.prior_reason: The assembly of peoples surrounding God and the request that He return on high remain in the judgment appeal. An identification with a particular heavenly ascent or named assembly is not established by the supplied words.

records.text: Righteous is my help from God, who saves those upright in heart.
records.prior_reason: God's help for the upright in heart is read as part of the appeal to the just judge; a further connection based only on the broad assurance of help to the righteous would be too general.

records.text: I will give thanks to the Lord according to His righteousness, and sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
records.prior_reason: Thanksgiving according to the Lord's righteousness and praise of the Most High conclude the psalm. Shared praise vocabulary or the divine title alone is not treated as an additional particular relationship.

records.text: For the end, concerning the hidden things of the son. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The heading concerning the hidden things of the son does not identify the son or explain the hidden things. Neither a historical child nor a christological referent is assumed from this title alone.

records.text: I will rejoice and exult in Thee; I will sing praise to Thy name, Most High.
records.prior_reason: The promise to rejoice, exult and praise the Most High is read, but repeated general praise language or the divine title alone does not establish a sufficiently particular additional target.

records.text: for Thou hast upheld my judgment and my cause; Thou sattest on a throne, Thou who judgest righteousness.
records.prior_reason: God's vindication of the speaker's case and righteous enthronement are read in context. No particular legal dispute is identified, and another generic judgment comparison is not added to the distinct throne-for-judgment link retained at 9:8.

records.text: The enemy’s swords failed utterly, and Thou didst pull down cities; their memory perished with a noise.
records.prior_reason: The failed enemy swords, demolished cities and vanished memory have no identified historical event in this psalm. A generic destroyed-city narrative would not establish the particular connection needed here.

records.text: Let those who know Thy name hope in Thee, for Thou hast not abandoned those who seek Thee, Lord.
records.prior_reason: The assurance that God has not abandoned those seeking Him and the call for name-knowers to hope are read, but no further distinct connection beyond generalized trust and nonabandonment is retained.

records.text: Appoint a lawgiver over them, Lord; let nations know that they are human beings. Diapsalma.
records.prior_reason: The request is to appoint a lawgiver so that nations know they are human. A familiar alternative rendering about terror is not substituted, and no particular lawgiver or matching episode is established.

records.text: As the ungodly man exalts himself, the poor man is set ablaze; they are caught in the counsels they devise.
records.prior_reason: The supplied line says the poor man is set ablaze as the ungodly exalts himself and describes entrapment in devised counsels. Its pronouns and burning image are not replaced with another edition's pursuit wording or forced into a named oppression event.

records.text: His ways are profaned at every time; Thy judgments are removed from before him; he will lord it over all his enemies.
records.prior_reason: The sinner's ways are said to be profaned, with divine judgments removed from before him and dominance over enemies. A prosperity rendering or a specific historical ruler is not imported to manufacture a connection.

records.text: In his trap he will humble him; he will bow down and fall as he lords it over the needy.
records.prior_reason: The trap, humbling, bowing and falling amid domination of the needy have potentially shifting pronouns. No target is retained by silently deciding which action belongs to oppressor or victim beyond what the source establishes.

records.text: Arise, Lord God; let Thy hand be raised; do not forget the needy.
records.prior_reason: The call for God to arise, raise His hand and remember the needy is read within the larger rebuttal of divine inattention. Another general arise-or-remember petition is not retained without an additional particular correspondence.

records.text: The Lord heard the desire of the needy; Thine ear attended to the preparation of their heart,
records.prior_reason: The hearing of the needy desire and attention to the heart's preparation are read as the prayer's answer. No sufficiently distinct target beyond generic hearing of prayer is established for this formulation.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David. In the Lord I have trusted. How will you say to my soul, “Move away to the mountains like a little bird”?
records.prior_reason: The title and running text together describe trust and advice to flee to the mountains like a little bird. The separately read Saul pursuit account contains a different night-raven comparison and does not establish this psalm's historical occasion.

records.text: For what Thou didst establish, they pulled down; but what did the righteous person do?
records.prior_reason: The text says opponents pulled down what God established and asks what the righteous person did. It does not explicitly name foundations, so that familiar formulation is not used to create an unsupported comparison.

records.text: For the Lord is righteous and loved righteous deeds; His face beheld uprightness.
records.prior_reason: The supplied declaration says the Lord loves righteous deeds and His face beheld uprightness. It is not rewritten as the upright seeing God's face, and no sufficiently particular additional counterpart is established for the actual formulation.

records.text: For the end, concerning the eighth. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The heading concerning the eighth and the David attribution are preserved; a repeated generic title alone does not receive a separate substantive connection.

records.text: Thou, Lord, wilt keep us and preserve us from this generation and for ever.
records.prior_reason: The assurance that the Lord will keep and preserve us from this generation and for ever is preserved; no more particular additional counterpart is retained beyond that common assurance of protection.

records.text: The ungodly walk around; according to Thy height, Thou heldest the sons of men in high regard.
records.prior_reason: The ungodly walking around and the Lord holding humanity in high regard according to His height are preserved without replacing the second clause with a familiar exaltation-of-vileness reading.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The generic liturgical heading is preserved without separate connection credit.

records.text: How long shall I place counsels within my soul, pains within my heart by day? How long will my enemy be raised above me?
records.prior_reason: The repeated questions about inner counsel, daily heart-pain and the enemy being raised remain distinct; no particular episode or additional counterpart is established.

records.text: You put a poor man’s counsel to shame, because the Lord is his hope.
records.prior_reason: The poor man’s shamed counsel and hope in the Lord are preserved; no specific counsel or historical poor person is identified by a generic poverty-and-hope comparison.

records.text: An inscription of David. Guard me, Lord, for I have hoped in Thee.
records.prior_reason: The inscription and plea for guarding because of hope in the Lord are preserved; no additional specific connection is retained from the general protection formula.

records.text: For the holy ones who are in His land, He made all His purposes wonderful among them.
records.prior_reason: The holy ones in His land and His wonderful purposes among them are not assigned a particular named group or event by analogy.

records.text: Their weaknesses multiplied; after these things they hurried. I will certainly not gather their gatherings of bloodshed, nor will I remember their names through my lips.
records.prior_reason: The gatherings of bloodshed and refusal to remember names remain as supplied. They are not rewritten as blood drink-offerings or assigned the identity of other gods; the naming comparison remains a separate zero-credit candidate.

records.text: I will bless the Lord, who gave me understanding; indeed, even until night my kidneys disciplined me.
records.prior_reason: The understanding given by the Lord and the kidneys’ discipline until night remain exact; no definite prophetic revelation or outside identity for that inward discipline is supplied.

records.text: so that my mouth might not speak human deeds. Because of the words of Thy lips, I kept hard paths.
records.prior_reason: Human deeds, words of God’s lips and hard paths are preserved without changing the hard paths into a familiar reference to paths of violent people.

records.text: I cried out, for Thou heardest me, God; incline Thine ear to me and hear my words.
records.prior_reason: Calling, being heard and asking for an inclined ear are preserved; the general prayer-attention formula alone receives no additional connection credit.

records.text: from the ungodly who made me miserable. My enemies surrounded my soul.
records.prior_reason: The enemies surrounding the speaker’s soul remain unnamed; a generic encirclement image does not identify a particular siege or hostile assembly.

records.text: They shut up their fat; their mouth spoke arrogance.
records.prior_reason: The statement that they shut up their fat is not silently converted into a description of unfeeling hearts; no particular counterpart to the complete wording is retained.

records.text: Casting me out, they now surrounded me; they set their eyes to turn aside toward the earth.
records.prior_reason: The eyes set to turn aside toward the earth are not rewritten into an explicit plan to throw the speaker to the ground; the exact relationship of the clauses remains unresolved.

records.text: Arise, Lord; get ahead of them and trip them up; rescue my soul from an ungodly man, Thy sword from the enemies of Thy hand.
records.prior_reason: The command to intercept and trip the enemies and the request concerning God’s sword are preserved. The ungodly man is not identified as God’s sword from a different familiar wording.

records.text: Lord, separate them from the few, from the earth, during their life. Their belly was filled with Thy hidden things; they were satisfied with sons and left the remains to their infants.
records.prior_reason: The few, earthly life, hidden things, filled belly, sons and remains for infants remain exact; they are not harmonized into a familiar statement that worldly people have their portion only in this life.

records.text: But I, in righteousness, will appear before Thy face; I will be satisfied when Thy glory appears.
records.prior_reason: Appearance before God in righteousness and satisfaction when His glory appears are preserved without adding awakening from death or identifying a particular resurrection event.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The generic heading supplies no separate substantive counterpart.

records.text: Day pours forth an utterance to day, and night announces knowledge to night.
records.prior_reason: Day’s utterance to day and night’s announcement to night remain the particular poetic sequence; a general creation-teaches motif does not establish an additional close counterpart in this pass.

records.text: There are no utterances or words whose voices are not heard.
records.prior_reason: The actual statement that there are no utterances or words whose voices are not heard is preserved. It is not changed into wordless or inaudible speech; the direct Romans quotation is retained for the following source unit.

records.text: For indeed, Thy servant keeps them; in keeping them there is great recompense.
records.prior_reason: The servant’s keeping and great recompense are preserved; no particular reward is identified from a generic obedience-and-blessing passage.

records.text: And spare Thy servant from others; if they do not rule over me, then I will be blameless and cleansed from great sin.
records.prior_reason: The source asks to be spared from others and their rule. Others is not silently replaced by presumptuous sins; the proposed comparison with Romans’ explicit rule of sin remains unresolved and earns zero credit.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The generic heading is preserved without a separate supported connection.

records.text: They were fettered and fell, but we rose and were set upright.
records.prior_reason: Their being fettered and falling, contrasted with our rising and being set upright, is preserved without identifying a particular battle or importing another passage’s named parties.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The generic heading is preserved without separate substantive connection credit.

records.text: His glory is great in Thy salvation; Thou wilt bestow glory and magnificence upon him.
records.prior_reason: The king’s glory, salvation and promised magnificence are preserved; a general statement that God grants honor does not furnish a particular additional match here.

records.text: May your hand be found by all your enemies; may your right hand find all who hate you.
records.prior_reason: The first clause asks that the addressed person’s hand be found by enemies; the second asks that the right hand find all who hate the addressee. Neither the direction of the first action nor the unspecified addressee is replaced by familiar wording.

records.text: Be exalted, Lord, in Thy power; we will sing and make music of Thy mighty acts.
records.prior_reason: The closing exaltation and promise of song for God’s mighty acts are preserved; generic praise of divine power alone is not counted as another particular connection.

records.text: For the end, concerning the help of the morning. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The title's morning-help designation is preserved; it does not establish a particular episode or a sufficiently specific independent connection.

records.text: But Thou dwellest among holy ones, the praise of Israel.
records.prior_reason: God's dwelling among holy ones and the praise of Israel are retained without identifying a particular heavenly assembly or earthly sanctuary.

records.text: Many calves surrounded me; fat bulls encompassed me.
records.prior_reason: The encircling calves and fat bulls are not identified with named historical attackers; a shared animal name would be insufficient.

records.text: I counted all my bones; but they observed and looked upon me.
records.prior_reason: Counting one's bones while others look upon the speaker does not establish John's separate not-broken-bone fulfillment; that proposed target remains uncredited.

records.text: This one will receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.
records.prior_reason: Receiving blessing and mercy follows the ethical entrance conditions; no sufficiently specific independent target beyond a general reward-for-righteousness theme is retained.

records.text: Who is this King of glory? The Lord of powers—He is the King of glory.
records.prior_reason: The Lord of powers is explicitly the King of glory, but an exact counterpart beyond general divine-kingship titles has not been established for this unit.

records.text: He will guide the meek in judgment; He will teach the meek His ways.
records.prior_reason: The guidance and teaching of the meek are preserved; promises of land to the meek do not by themselves establish this different instructional relationship.

records.text: See my humiliation and my toil, and forgive all my sins.
records.prior_reason: The joined appeal to see humiliation and toil and forgive all sins has not been given an independent target on the strength of generic forgiveness language alone.

records.text: Innocent and upright people clung to me, for I waited for Thee, Lord.
records.prior_reason: The innocent and upright clinging to the speaker do not identify particular companions; generic fellowship among the virtuous is insufficient here.

records.text: For Thy mercy is before my eyes, and I acted pleasingly in Thy truth.
records.prior_reason: Mercy before the eyes and conduct pleasing in truth are preserved; no particular act or independent textual counterpart has been established.

records.text: to hear a voice of praise and recount all Thy wonders.
records.prior_reason: Hearing praise and recounting wonders remain this worshiping purpose; a general command to praise or recount God's deeds is insufficient for a retained pair.

records.text: But I walked in my innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me.
records.prior_reason: Walking in innocence and asking redemption and mercy are preserved without treating every innocence or redemption prayer as a specific counterpart.

records.text: When those doing evil approached me to eat my flesh, those who afflict me and my enemies, they grew weak and fell.
records.prior_reason: The flesh-devouring attackers' collapse is not identified with a particular military or Passion episode; that identity requires more than approaching enemies falling.

records.text: And now, behold, He raised my head above my enemies; I went around and sacrificed in His tent a sacrifice of shouting; I will sing and make music to the Lord.
records.prior_reason: The lifted head and sacrifice of shouting in the tent do not establish a particular triumphal sacrifice elsewhere.

records.text: Hear, Lord, my voice with which I cried; have mercy on me and hear me.
records.prior_reason: The cry for hearing and mercy has no sufficiently particular independent link retained beyond a general prayer formula.

records.text: The Lord is my helper and my protector; in Him my heart hoped, and I was helped, and my flesh blossomed anew; from my own will I will thank Him.
records.prior_reason: The heart's hope, help and flesh blossoming anew are preserved without equating the bodily image with a specific healing or resurrection narrative.

records.text: and He will grind them fine—Lebanon like the calf— and the beloved like a young one-horned animal.
records.prior_reason: The text says Lebanon, the calf and the beloved like a young one-horned animal; it does not explicitly name Hermon or Sanior, and that geographic identification remains uncredited.

records.text: The voice of the Lord, who cleaves a flame of fire.
records.prior_reason: The voice cleaving a flame of fire is not silently rewritten as lightning; no sufficiently precise independent counterpart has been retained.

records.text: The voice of the Lord, who makes deer ready; and He will uncover forests; in His temple everyone speaks glory.
records.prior_reason: Making deer ready does not expressly state childbirth in the supplied wording; the proposed birth-pain comparison remains uncredited, and general temple praise supplies no separate retained link.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of a song for the dedication of the house. Of David.
records.prior_reason: The Davidic title names dedication of the house without identifying the house or occasion; Solomon's later dedication is not assigned as its event.

records.text: To Thee, Lord, I will cry, and to my God I will make my petition:
records.prior_reason: The future cry and petition do not establish an independent specific relationship beyond the general act of prayer.

records.text: so that my glory may sing praise unto Thee, and I may certainly not be pierced with grief. Lord my God, I will thank Thee for ever.
records.prior_reason: Perpetual thanksgiving and freedom from grief remain this conclusion; a generic perpetual-praise verse is not retained as a specific counterpart.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David, of alarm.
records.prior_reason: The title of alarm is not assigned to a particular event in David's life without textual identification.

records.text: But I hoped in Thee, Lord; I said, “Thou art my God.”
records.prior_reason: The declaration of hope and Thou art my God is preserved without making every profession of trust an independent cross-reference.

records.text: Lord, may I not be put to shame, for I called upon Thee; may the ungodly be ashamed and brought down to Hades.
records.prior_reason: The contrasting pleas about shame and Hades do not identify a particular enemy's fate; general punishment language is insufficient for a retained link.

records.text: How great is the multitude of Thy kindness, Lord, which Thou didst conceal for those who fear Thee, which Thou didst accomplish for those who hope in Thee before the sons of men!
records.prior_reason: Kindness concealed for those fearing God and accomplished for those hoping in Him is not identified with a particular promised treasure or later revelation.

records.text: Blessed be the Lord, because He made His mercy wonderful in an enclosed city.
records.prior_reason: The enclosed city is unnamed; the proposed identification with Keilah is not established and receives no credit.

records.text: Love the Lord, all His holy ones, because the Lord seeks truths and repays those who act with abundant arrogance.
records.prior_reason: Love for the Lord and His repayment of abundant arrogance are not attached to a specific arrogant ruler or incident.

records.text: Thou art my refuge from the affliction surrounding me; my exultation, redeem me from those who have encircled me. Diapsalma.
records.prior_reason: The refuge and redemption from surrounding affliction do not identify a particular siege or escape; generic rescue imagery alone is not retained.

records.text: May Thy mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in Thee.
records.prior_reason: The closing appeal for mercy according to hope is not given a target on the basis of mercy and hope alone.

records.text: Of David, when he altered his face before Abimelech, who dismissed him, and he went away.
records.prior_reason: The title names Abimelech in the altered-face episode. The checked Samuel account names Achish. The episode identification and equivalence of those names are not established by the supplied passages.

records.text: The death of sinners is evil, and those who hate the righteous will incur guilt.
records.prior_reason: The bad death of sinners and guilt of those hating the righteous need a particular supported comparison. The inspected Proverbs14:32 text concerns being thrust away in wickedness and trust in piety, without the expected death wording; it is not substituted for another edition.

records.text: But against me they rejoiced and gathered; scourges gathered against me, and I did not know; they were torn apart and felt no remorse.
records.prior_reason: The gathering and rejoicing of opponents is clear, but the supplied phrases about scourges gathering and being torn apart without remorse are not silently rewritten. No adequately particular target for the complete complaint was established.

records.text: Thou hast seen, Lord; do not remain silent. Lord, do not depart from me.
records.prior_reason: The request that the God who has seen not remain silent or depart is read within the hostile-witness lament. A broad comparison to divine awareness or rescue alone does not establish a sufficiently distinctive retained link in this pass.

records.text: For he acted deceitfully in his sight, as to finding his lawlessness and hating it.
records.prior_reason: The formulation acted deceitfully in his sight, as to finding his lawlessness and hating it leaves the precise relation of self-deception and recognition unresolved. No explanatory paraphrase replacing that wording is credited.

records.text: Let a foot of arrogance not come against me; let a hand of sinners not shake me.
records.prior_reason: The prayer against an arrogant foot and a shaking hand of sinners is preserved. General opposition to pride or petitions for protection do not supply a sufficiently particular checked target for these images in this pass.

records.text: For I hoped in Thee, Lord; Thou wilt hear, Lord my God.
records.prior_reason: The speaker's hope and assurance that the Lord will hear are preserved. The checked Psalm39 testimony contains patient waiting and divine hearing, but these common prayer responses alone do not establish a sufficiently particular correspondence; that proposal remains a separate pending candidate.

records.text: For I am ready for scourges, and my pain is continually before me.
records.prior_reason: Readiness for scourges and continual pain are preserved as written. A suggested resemblance to continual consciousness of sin would substitute a different object for pain, so no such comparison is retained.

records.text: Do not abandon me, Lord; my God, do not depart from me.
records.prior_reason: The request not to be abandoned or have God depart is preserved within this suffering lament. Psalm21 similarly requests divine nearness in affliction, but that common presence petition alone is insufficiently particular; the proposed comparison remains pending.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The general for-the-end and Davidic psalm heading supplies no distinctive event or recipient here. General evidence that Davidic words were sung does not identify this particular poem and receives no completion credit.

records.text: I waited patiently for the Lord; He attended to me and heard my supplication.
records.prior_reason: Patient waiting, divine attention and the hearing of supplication are preserved as the speaker's testimony. The checked Psalm33 passage describes seeking and rescue from sojourns; the general resemblance of prayer being heard does not establish a sufficiently particular counterpart to this waiting account.

records.text: For the end. A psalm of David.
records.prior_reason: The general for-the-end and Davidic psalm heading has no distinctive event or named recipient. Shared Davidic authorship alone is not credited as an additional curated match.
